target_customer: B2B marketplaces, merchants and distributors that sell to businesses and want net terms and online checkout
problem: Business buyers pay by check and invoice on net terms, so sellers wait for cash and have no consumer style checkout.
business_model: Payment and trade credit fees on B2B transactions plus software fees
product_category: B2B payments, checkout and trade credit infrastructure

founders.name: Bar Geron
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Feb 2021 says he met Shuster at PayPal and later worked at Behalf, a B2B financing company.

founders.name: Yoni Shuster
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he stayed at PayPal when Geron left. Education not found.

competitors.name: Behalf
competitors.what: B2B financing offering net payment terms without digitizing the payment model

technical_complexity.rationale: Checkout and invoicing are standard, but underwriting trade credit and funding net terms need risk models and capital.

defensibility.rationale: Embedded checkout and buyer credit data raise switching costs, while lending needs capital that few rivals have.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Stripe became an investor rather than a rival. No acquisition found through 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Feb 2021 describes B2B payments as analog, with checks and invoices, while pandemic ecommerce grew. Balance claimed to serve large brands later.

branding.domain_note: Uses getbalance.com, suggesting balance.com was unavailable; not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as Stripe for B2B with a consumer like business checkout

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered funding, not the brand. The name is a common word that competes with many fintech names, but customers like Instacart and Upwork lend credibility.

outcome_analysis: Balance raised $5.5M seed in February 2021, $25M Series A in August 2021, $56M Series B in July 2022 and a $350M credit facility in November 2022, then widened from checkout to trade credit and receivables tools. Named customers include Instacart, Upwork and GE Vernova. It stays active with 70 staff. Investor backing from Stripe and Ribbit and a funded credit line signal real demand, though revenue is not public.
notes: CB Insights and another profile list total funding near $436M, which likely includes debt; unverified. The Series B total of $87M is from one outlet. The Balance blog also states the $350M facility. Competitor source is Feb 2021, about six months after the batch. Name origin not found.
